text:
Which of the following compounds can be
prepared in good yield by Gabriel phthalimide
synthesis?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is a method used to prepare primary aliphatic and aromatic amines. The process begins with phthalimide being treated with ethanolic potassium hydroxide (KOH), forming the potassium salt of phthalimide. This salt is then heated with an alkyl halide (RX), and subsequent treatment with either alkaline hydrolysis or hydrazinolysis (using hydrazine, $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{N}\cdot \mathrm{NH}_{2}$) yields the corresponding primary amine. However, this method cannot be used to synthesize primary aromatic amines that have electron-withdrawing groups (EWGs) at the ortho- and para-positions, such as the nitro group ($-\mathrm{NO}_{2}$). This limitation arises because aryl halides (ArX) do not undergo nucleophilic substitution ($\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}$) reactions with the anion formed by phthalimide.

text:
The average molar mass of chlorine is
35.5 g mol$^{–1}$. The ratio of $^{35}Cl$ to $^{37}Cl$ in naturally
occuring chlorine is close to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the mole ratio of ${}^{35}\text{Cl}$ to ${}^{37}\text{Cl}$ be $x:y$. The average molar mass is the mole-weighted mean:

$35.5=\dfrac{35x+37y}{x+y}$

$35.5x+35.5y=35x+37y\Rightarrow 0.5x=1.5y$

$\dfrac{x}{y}=\dfrac{1.5}{0.5}=3$

So ${}^{35}\text{Cl}:{}^{37}\text{Cl}=3:1$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot

text:
For the given cell :

$Cu(s) | Cu^{2+}(C_{1}M) || Cu^{2+}(C_{2}M) | Cu(s)$

change in Gibbs energy ($\Delta$G) is negative, if :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $\Delta$G  0

We know, $E_{$cell} = $E_{cell}^{0}$ - $\frac{RT}{2F}\ln \left (\frac{C_{1}}{C_{2}}\right )$

 = 0 - $\frac{RT}{2F}\ln \left (\frac{C_{1}}{C_{2}}\right )$

$\therefore$ - $\frac{RT}{2F}\ln \left (\frac{C_{1}}{C_{2}}\right )$ > 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\ln \left (\frac{C_{1}}{C_{2}}\right )$ < 0

$\Rightarrow$ $C_{1} < C_{2}$

By checking option, we can see

$C_{2} =$ $\sqrt{2}C_{1}$ satisfy the condition $C_{1} < C_{2}$.

text:
A set of solutions is prepared using 180 g of
water as a solvent and 10 g of different nonvolatile solutes A, B and C. The relative
lowering of vapour pressure in the presence of
these solutes are in the order :

[Given, molar
mass of A = 100 g mol$^{–1}$; B = 200 g mol$^{–1}$;
C = 10,000 g mol$^{–1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Relative lowering in vapour pressure (RLVP)

= $\frac{P-P_{s}}{P}=\frac{n}{n+N}$

n $\to$ moles of solute

N $\to$ moles of solvent

$\therefore$ (RLVP$)_{A} =$ $\frac{\frac{10}{100}}{\frac{10}{100}+\frac{180}{18}}$

(RLVP$)_{B} =$ $\frac{\frac{10}{200}}{\frac{10}{200}+\frac{180}{18}}$

and (RLVP$)_{C} =$ $\frac{\frac{10}{10000}}{\frac{10}{10000}+\frac{180}{18}}$

$\therefore$ (RLVP$)_{A} > ($RLVP$)_{B} > ($RLVP$)_{C}$

So, A > B > C
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot

text:
For $a d^{4}$ metal ion in an octahedral field, the
correct electronic configuration is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a $d^{4}$ ion in an octahedral field, the first three electrons occupy the $t_{2g}$ orbitals singly. The fourth electron either pairs in $t_{2g}$, costing the pairing energy $P$, or enters $e_{g}$, costing $\Delta _{o}$.

When $\Delta _{o}<P$ (weak field), entering $e_{g}$ costs less, so the configuration is high spin, $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{1}$.


[IMG]

When $\Delta _{o}>P$ (strong field), the electron pairs in $t_{2g}$ to give $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{0}$; options (A) and (B) pair each configuration with the opposite condition, and (C) fills $e_{g}$ before $t_{2g}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 6th September Evening Slot
